explain.say: George Washington Carver had an answer. Born enslaved around 1864, he became a great plant scientist at Tuskegee Institute. Look at the next box: he told farmers to plant peanuts, beans or sweet potatoes some years. This is called crop rotation, which means taking turns with crops.

faq.a: An African American scientist and teacher, born enslaved around 1864 in Missouri. At Tuskegee Institute in Alabama, he helped poor farmers save their soil and grow better crops.
asks: Where did George Washington Carver work?

faq.a: Growing different crops in a field in different years, taking turns, so the soil stays healthy and pests do not build up.

faq.q: How do peanuts help the soil?
faq.a: Peanuts are legumes. Bacteria living in bumps on their roots take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the next crop.

faq.q: Did George Washington Carver invent peanut butter?
faq.a: No. People in South America ground peanuts into paste long ago, and peanut butter was sold before his work. He did find about 300 uses for peanuts.
A school on wheels that Carver helped start in 1906. It carried tools and lessons out to farmers who could not travel to college.

facts: George Washington Carver began teaching at Tuskegee Institute in Alabama in 1896.
Peanuts are legumes, which host root bacteria that add nitrogen to the soil.
